cases.input: What's the weather in San Francisco today? Give the high in Fahrenheit.
cases.note: Grades the PRESENCE of a temperature figure, and nothing more. The pattern accepts both the degree glyph ('68°') and the spelled-out unit ('68 degrees Fahrenheit', '68 deg F'), because the graders case-fold but never map glyph to word (models.py:64-75); before #620 a correct plain-English answer was punished for using the word instead of the symbol. NOT FALSIFIABLE -- measured, not assumed (#1602). This note used to claim the case was falsifiable: that an agent unable to fetch a matching forecast follows the SKILL rule, refuses with no figure, and reds the grader. Two nightly cluster-rung runs on 2026-08-17 disprove it. Run 32019827183 (forecast-host egress opened, the fetch still blocked) and run 32019884344 (the same allowance deliberately pointed at TEST-NET-1, so NO source was reachable at all) BOTH passed. The model does not refuse: it reports the search-summary numbers behind an explicit caveat ('These numbers came from search-result summaries, not pages I was able to open and verify myself'), and that caveated answer still carries a temperature figure, so the regex matches. RESIDUAL LIMITS: (1) this case cannot grade PROVENANCE -- an agent that invents or search-summarizes a plausible temperature ('72 degrees') passes exactly like one that fetched and date-matched a page. (2) That gap is nobody's scope yet -- NOT #618, which closed 2026-07-17 and pointed the other way (a false NEGATIVE: the regex punished the spelled-out unit). Closing it needs the semantic verifier grader (GraderKind.verifier, ADR-0042, itself blocked on ADR-0022 Phase 1), which no member of the frozen exact|contains|regex taxonomy can express. #620 is only the false-negative stopgap. Until then, read a green here as 'the turn completed and produced a number', never as 'the SKILL's fetch-and-date-match rule was followed'.
